title: House Robber
source: canonical House Robber concept; description, examples, and tests re-authored
description: The input is an array of non-negative integers, the value kept in a row of houses. Choose values so that no two chosen values sit at adjacent positions in the array. Return the largest total that can be chosen.
hints: At each position the choice is binary: take it (and forget the previous one) or skip it.
Two rolling totals are enough: the best total if you took the current value versus the best if you skipped it.
Walk the array once with take = skip + value and skip = max(skip, old take); answer with the larger.
solution: Rolling pair over the array: taking the current value adds it to the best total ending two positions back; skipping keeps the better of the previous two totals. O(n) time, O(1) space.
failureHint: hidden tests include a single house, two houses, and values where skipping a big one wins

visible.failNote: adjacent positions cannot both be taken
the best pair is not always the biggest value plus a neighbor
